brief: Verdict ahead of the print: Helios has turned from a construction project into a rent-paying asset, but the market is pricing the tenant, not the building. Expect the quarter to confirm Phase I's economics; the stock will move on what Galaxy says about CoreWeave exposure, Phase III funding and the 830 MW.

Where expectations sit. EPS consensus ranges from -$0.13 (Zacks, 13 October, stale) to +$0.04 (Yahoo, 22 October, 14 analysts, range -$0.44 to +$0.49), with Benzinga at -$0.06; revisions are moving up (Yahoo -$0.08 thirty days ago). That compares with -$0.09 in 2Q26 and $1.12 adjusted a year ago. Revenue consensus ($9.04bn or $8.58bn) is gross crypto trading revenue and says nothing about earnings power. We found no adjusted EBITDA or Data Centers consensus, so management's guide is the bar: about $80mn of Phase I leasing revenue a quarter at a project-level margin above 90%. Bitcoin rose about 43% in the quarter, so the Treasury and Corporate marks should help, though some holdings are carried under impairment accounting.

Helios economics. Phase I: 133 MW, cost $1.8bn, $315mn average annual base revenue (about $197 per kW-month, a 17.5% average yield on cost). Contracted minimum cash rent is lower in the early years: $259.1mn in 2027, or about $162 per kW-month. The $80mn quarterly figure is straight-line revenue. Phase II: 260 MW, estimated cost $4.0bn, $690mn average revenue, 13.7% starting yield, funded by the 9.875% notes. On Galaxy's own schedule, debt service coverage is only about 1.2x to 1.3x in 2029 to 2031, and about $3.05-3.2bn of notes remain at the August 2031 maturity ($3,215mn at end-2030, $3,048mn at end-2031). Phase III (133 MW, 2028) still needs debt; at Phase II costs that is roughly a $2bn build (our estimate).

Three debates. First, CoreWeave: all 526 MW rests on one tenant whose CDS is about 1,100bp; what security protects Galaxy and its noteholders? Second, funding: Phase III debt, $445mn of 2026 exchangeable notes maturing within weeks (exchange price about $33, stock about $17), $1.49bn of open construction commitments, and an unused $500mn ATM. Third, Helios II: Citi expects a tenant within six months, but power arrives in late 2028 and Texas has paused new large-load approvals until mid-December.

What would move the stock. Positive: rent at or above the guide with cash collection disclosed, named tenant security or a stronger-credit backstop, a Helios II lease with an investment-grade tenant or wrap, and Phase III debt with no equity. Negative: any change to CoreWeave lease terms, equity issuance near $17, a Phase III cost or schedule slip, or silence on tenant protections.

Kona read-through. A neocloud's credit passes straight through to its landlord's equity and bonds, even while rent is being paid. Kona should require security that survives a tenant restructuring before committing capex for a single neocloud tenant. Galaxy's late-2028 grid power also shows the value of faster off-grid time-to-power.
changes: Phase I (133 MW) is in service: management guides about $80mn of quarterly leasing revenue at a project-level margin above 90% from 3Q26, against $18.9mn of lease revenue in the 2Q26 ramp quarter.

Phase II is funded by $3.507bn of 9.875% senior secured notes due August 2031 (closed 28 July), at an 85% loan-to-cost per the call (87.7% against the $4.0bn estimated cost) with an uncapped completion guarantee from the parent partnership; first halls are due 2Q27.
CoreWeave's credit has sold off: five-year CDS about 1,100bp and 2032 notes at 80.5 cents (14.7%). GLXY fell 31% from the end of September to 19 October, in step with CRWV.
The Texas audit has paused ERCOT's Batch Zero until mid-December, which holds back Helios III and the new sites; Helios II (830 MW, approved) energizes in late 2028 and has no tenant.

Bitcoin rose about 43% in the quarter and EPS estimates are moving up: consensus runs from -$0.13 (Zacks, 13 Oct, stale) to +$0.04 (Yahoo, 22 Oct, 14 analysts), with Benzinga at -$0.06; Yahoo's figure was -$0.01 seven days ago and -$0.08 thirty days ago.

consensus_thesis: Investors own Galaxy as a crypto franchise with a contracted Helios annuity underneath; at $16.93 the price roughly equals contracted Helios value, so the debate is whether CoreWeave's credit stress makes that annuity worth less than the sell side assumes.
headline: 3Q26 is the first full quarter of Helios rent, but the stock will trade on CoreWeave's credit: investors want to know whether the roughly $80mn-a-quarter Phase I annuity and the debt-funded Phase II and III build hold up for a landlord whose only tenant's bonds now yield about 15%.
kona: Galaxy shows that a neocloud's credit passes straight through to its landlord. Rent is being paid on time, yet GLXY fell 31% with CoreWeave, and the 9.875% Helios II debt priced before the tenant's bonds fell to about 15%. Kona, at tens of MW, should not commit capex for a single neocloud tenant without security that survives a tenant restructuring: prepayments, letters of credit, or a guarantee from a stronger party. Galaxy's 830 MW of approved grid power is still unleased because it energizes in late 2028 and Texas has gated large loads, which supports Kona's time-to-power case if its gas permits move faster than an ERCOT queue.

name: Galaxy Digital

questions.question: Your 10-Q shows contracted minimum lease income of $126.9mn for 2H26, about $63mn a quarter, and $259.1mn for 2027, yet you guide about $80mn a quarter of leasing revenue, so roughly $15mn a quarter is straight-line accrual. What cash rent did CoreWeave pay in 3Q26, is it current on every payment, and how large is the straight-line receivable at 30 September? Will you report cash rent collected every quarter from now on?
questions.why: Tests pillar 1. With CoreWeave's CDS near 1,100bp, cash collection and a growing receivable are the first signs of tenant stress, and the gap between accrual and cash is what a bondholder would watch.

questions.question: The Helios II notes priced at 9.875% at what you called an 85% loan-to-cost (87.7% against the $4.0bn estimated cost), and your offering deck shows debt service coverage of only 1.22x in 2029, while CoreWeave's 2032 notes now trade at 80.5 cents. What tenant security exists across Phases I to III (deposits, letters of credit, guarantees), and in what dollar amount? If CoreWeave rejected the leases in a restructuring, how long would re-leasing take and at what rent? Yes or no: is any part of the CoreWeave obligation backed by an investment-grade party?
questions.why: Tests pillar 3. A thin coverage ratio leaves little room for a rent cut. Recovery depends on security and on re-leasing value, not on the headline lease value.

questions.question: Phase III still needs its debt, and at Phase II's roughly $15.4mn per MW it is about a $2bn build. At what loan-to-cost and coupon do you expect to close it now that CoreWeave-tenant debt has repriced, and by what date must it close to hold rent commencement in 2028? Your deck also leaves about $3.05-3.2bn of Helios II notes outstanding at the August 2031 maturity. What remaining lease term will back that refinancing?
questions.why: Tests pillar 2 and the no-equity promise. A wider spread on Phase III, or a 2031 refinancing against a shorter remaining lease, cuts equity returns or pushes the parent into the funding.

questions.question: $445mn of 2026 exchangeable notes matures in 2026, within weeks, at an exchange price of about $33.34, against a share price of $16.93, and $1.49bn of Helios construction commitments are open. Will you repay from the $2.46bn of cash and stablecoins, refinance, or draw on the $500mn ATM, and did you sell any ATM shares in 3Q26? How much of that cash does the trading business need to keep?
questions.why: With the stock down 31% in three weeks, the choice between cash and equity sets dilution risk for shareholders and liquidity cover for creditors.

questions.question: Citi expects a Helios II tenant within six months, but you said energization is slated for late 2028 and ERCOT's audit runs to about 10 December. Do you have an LOI or exclusivity on any of the 830 MW, and with what kind of counterparty? Would you lease to another neocloud only with an investment-grade wrap? Will you sign before Helios III's Batch Zero status is known?
questions.why: Tests pillar 4. A second tenant with stronger credit is the cleanest answer to the concentration discount, while another unwrapped neocloud would deepen it.

sections.body: Galaxy has two engines. The crypto franchise (trading, lending, asset management, staking) and the Treasury book drive reported earnings and swing with digital asset prices. The data center business is a single-tenant landlord at Helios in West Texas: 526 MW of critical IT leased to CoreWeave on near-triple-net 15-year leases with 3-5% escalators. Each phase sits in its own project subsidiary with secured debt, so equity returns depend on yield on cost (about 14-17%) exceeding the cost of debt (8.7% on the Phase I loan; 9.875% on the Phase II notes), and on CoreWeave paying.
